issues.legal_issue: An ancestral estate that is impartible by custom and descends by primogeniture remains joint family property, although most ordinary coparcenary rights do not apply to it.
material_facts: The estate was ancestral and descended by primogeniture under a family custom.
The family remained undivided when the estate was held as impartible.
The dispute arose in a partition suit concerning the family estate.
issues.conclusion: The estate was not the holder’s separate or exclusive property; it remained joint family property, with survivorship as the relevant continuing coparcenary right.
issues.legal_principle: Under Shiba Prasad Singh v. Rani Prayag Kumari Debi, an ancestral customary impartible estate descending by primogeniture remains joint family property. The rights of partition, restraint of alienation, and maintenance do not apply in the ordinary way to impartible property, but survivorship remains; that right is distinct from a mere spes successionis and may be renounced or surrendered. Rani Sartaj Kuari v. Deoraj Kuari and the First Pittapur case address the incompatibility of partition and restraint of alienation with impartibility, while the Second Pittapur case addresses maintenance.

rule.if: partition_proceeding and ancestral_estate and impartibility_by_custom and descent_by_primogeniture

predicates.partition_proceeding: The dispute is being determined in a proceeding seeking partition of family property.
predicates.ancestral_estate: The property came down through the family as ancestral property.
predicates.impartibility_by_custom: The family custom treated the estate as indivisible.
predicates.descent_by_primogeniture: The estate descended to a single heir under a primogeniture rule.

issues.definition: When a partition proceeding concerns an ancestral estate treated as indivisible by custom and descended by primogeniture, the estate remains joint family property.

issues.legal_issue: A holder of a customary impartible estate may incorporate subsequently acquired immovable property into it by demonstrating an intention to do so, and property incorporated before the governing enactment is included in the scheduled estate.
material_facts: The estate was a customary impartible estate included in the schedule to the earlier enactment.
The holder had acquired immovable property after the original grant and before the enactment.
The parties disputed whether scheduled-estate status was confined to the property described in the original grant.
issues.conclusion: The enactment did not confine the estate to the original grant; immovable property incorporated into the estate before the enactment could form part of the scheduled estate, with incorporation determined on the facts of each property.
issues.legal_principle: Shiba Prasad Singh v. Rani Prayag Kumari Debi establishes that, unless excluded by statute or custom, a holder of a customary impartible estate may incorporate self-acquired immovable property by declaring an intention to do so. Incorporation turns on intention, which may be established by conduct or other evidence. Sections 2(2), 2(3), and 3 of the Madras Impartible Estates Act, 1904 did not restrict the scheduled estate to the original grant; property incorporated before that Act could form an integral part of the scheduled estate. The principle does not apply to movable property, which may be impartible only if a family custom to that effect is proved.

rule.if: customary_impartible_estate and subsequently_acquired_immovable_property and incorporation_intended and incorporation_before_enactment

predicates.customary_impartible_estate: The estate is treated as indivisible under a family custom.
predicates.subsequently_acquired_immovable_property: The holder acquired immovable property after the original estate had been granted.
predicates.incorporation_intended: The holder's declaration, conduct, or other evidence shows an intention to make the acquisition part of the impartible estate.
predicates.incorporation_before_enactment: The holder's incorporation of the property occurred before the enactment governing the scheduled estate.

issues.definition: A subsequently acquired immovable property intended to be incorporated into a customary impartible estate before the relevant enactment is included in that scheduled estate.

issues.legal_issue: A family’s members cannot claim under the building-vesting provision merely because they have a joint-family interest in an impartible estate when the holder owned the building immediately before the notified date.
material_facts: The buildings at issue were outside the categories governed by the first three subsections of the building-vesting provision.
The estate holder possessed the impartible estate immediately before the notified date.
Other family members claimed that their joint-family interests made them owners of the buildings for the purpose of the remaining subsection.
issues.conclusion: The remaining subsection vested the buildings in the landholder, not in the other family members, and those members could not claim its benefit on the basis of their joint-family interest.
issues.legal_principle: Section 18(4) of the Madras Estates (Abolition and Conversion into Ryotwari) Act, 1948 vests a building in the person who owned it immediately before the notified date. Read with sections 2(8), 2(12), 43, and 45(2)(a) and (b), the expression refers to the landholder or proprietor, not to all members of the family who have a theoretical joint-family interest in an impartible estate. The broader construction would anomalously give a wider group rights in buildings than the class entitled to claim apportionment of compensation.

rule.if: vesting_proceeding and building_outside_first_three_categories and holder_owned_building_before_vesting and claimants_are_other_family_members

predicates.vesting_proceeding: The dispute concerns who receives a building under a statutory vesting arrangement following the taking over of an estate.
predicates.building_outside_first_three_categories: The building does not fall within any of the first three statutory categories for buildings.
predicates.holder_owned_building_before_vesting: The estate holder owned the building immediately before the relevant vesting date.
predicates.claimants_are_other_family_members: The persons claiming the building are family members other than the estate holder.

issues.definition: When the holder owned a building before vesting and the claimants are other family members, those claimants cannot obtain it under the residual building-vesting provision.

issues.legal_issue: A market built on estate land by an estate holder as a public amenity may be found to have been incorporated into the customary impartible estate when the evidence supports that intention.
material_facts: The market was built by an estate holder on land admittedly belonging to the estate.
The market was constructed to provide a public amenity to the town associated with the estate.
The market was treated in the estate’s accounts and administration as connected with the estate.
Both lower courts found that the market had been incorporated.
issues.conclusion: The finding that the market formed part of the impartible estate was upheld.
issues.legal_principle: Under Shiba Prasad Singh v. Rani Prayag Kumari Debi, incorporation of acquired immovable property depends on the holder’s intention, inferred from the evidence and conduct. Whether a particular property was incorporated is a question of fact; the courts considered the market’s location on estate land, its public purpose, and its treatment in administration, and the Supreme Court found no basis to disturb the concurrent conclusion.

rule.if: partition_appeal and acquired_property_is_immovable and property_built_on_estate_land and holder_created_public_amenity and concurrent_findings_support_incorporation

predicates.partition_appeal: The matter is an appeal arising from a partition dispute over family property.
predicates.acquired_property_is_immovable: The disputed acquisition is immovable property obtained after the original estate was constituted.
predicates.property_built_on_estate_land: The holder built the property on land already belonging to the estate.
predicates.holder_created_public_amenity: The holder constructed the property to provide a public amenity rather than as a private profit-making venture.
predicates.concurrent_findings_support_incorporatio: The courts below both found incorporation on evidence of the holder's intention and treatment of the property.

issues.definition: In a partition appeal, an immovable public amenity built on estate land may remain part of the impartible estate when the findings support the holder's intention to incorporate it.

issues.legal_issue: A leasehold interest recovered for the estate through a settlement and treated by the holder and estate administration as an estate accretion may be incorporated into the impartible estate.
material_facts: The villages had originally formed part of the estate and were later sold for arrears.
A settlement resulted in permanent leasehold rights in the villages being held through a nominee of the estate.
The estate holder guaranteed the lease arrangement and actively dealt with it as his own interest.
The estate’s trust deed and later administrative conduct treated the leasehold rights as part of the estate.
issues.conclusion: The permanent leasehold rights were properly treated as forming part of the impartible estate.
issues.legal_principle: The governing incorporation principle, stated in Shiba Prasad Singh v. Rani Prayag Kumari Debi, requires proof of intention and permits that intention to be inferred from conduct. The settlement, the holder’s active involvement and guarantee, the nominee arrangement, and later treatment of the leasehold interest supported the factual conclusion that it was an accretion to the estate.

rule.if: partition_appeal and estate_accretion_claim and leasehold_rights_recovered_for_estate and holder_treated_rights_as_estate_property and estate_administration_confirmed_that_treatment

predicates.partition_appeal: The matter is an appeal arising from a partition dispute over family property.
predicates.estate_accretion_claim: A party claims that an acquired or recovered property interest became part of an impartible estate.
predicates.leasehold_rights_recovered_for_estate: Leasehold rights over property formerly belonging to the estate were obtained through an arrangement made for the estate.
predicates.holder_treated_rights_as_estate_property: The holder actively handled the transaction and treated the rights as belonging to the estate.
predicates.estate_administration_confirmed_that_tre: The estate's trust arrangements or later administration also treated the rights as part of the estate.

issues.definition: Leasehold rights recovered for an estate and consistently treated by the holder and its administration as estate property form part of the impartible estate.

issues.legal_issue: A family custom may make identified ceremonial movable property impartible, and the custom may continue after the circumstances that gave rise to it have changed.
material_facts: The dispute concerned jewels alleged to be regalia and therefore unavailable for partition.
Family documents and conduct before and after an adoption showed that certain ceremonial jewels were treated as state regalia and family heirlooms.
An earlier family member described specified jewels as regalia, and a later list recorded jewels taken out for an installation ceremony.
The family’s treatment of ceremonial jewels continued after the estate was abolished.
The lower appellate court identified 38 jewels as regalia, and the Supreme Court found no sufficient basis to disturb that factual conclusion.
issues.conclusion: The 38 identified jewels were properly treated as regalia and excluded from partition as impartible property.
issues.legal_principle: Movable property cannot become part of an impartible estate through the doctrine of incorporation; a family custom of impartibility must be proved. Ramalakshmi Ammal v. Sivanantha Perumal Sethurayar requires clear and unambiguous proof that a custom is ancient and invariable. For a family custom, the family’s consensus, traditional belief, statements, and conduct are relevant; Abdul Hussain Khan v. Bibi Sona Daro is cited on proof of family custom. Shiba Prasad Singh v. Rani Prayag Kumari Debi states the broader law of impartible estates. Rai Kishore Singh v. Mst. Gahenabai supports the principle that a custom may outlive the condition that gave rise to it. The evidence supported the continuing family custom and the identification of the ceremonial jewels.

rule.if: partition_proceeding and movable_property_claimed_as_regalia and family_consistently_treated_ceremonial_items_as_regalia and custom_continued_after_change_in_circumstances and evidence_clearly_proves_custom

predicates.partition_proceeding: The dispute is being determined in a proceeding seeking partition of family property.
predicates.movable_property_claimed_as_regalia: A party claims that movable family property is ceremonial regalia and is not available for partition.
predicates.family_consistently_treated_ceremonial_i: Family members treated the relevant ceremonial items as regalia in documents and conduct over time.
predicates.custom_continued_after_change_in_circums: The family continued to observe the practice after the circumstances associated with its origin had changed.
predicates.evidence_clearly_proves_custom: The evidence of family belief, statements, and conduct clearly establishes the claimed custom.

issues.definition: Ceremonial movable items are impartible when clear evidence shows that a family consistently treated them as regalia and continued that practice after circumstances changed.

issues.legal_issue: A holder’s acquisition and use of buildings for personal convenience do not establish incorporation into an impartible estate where the evidence of intention is ambiguous, and a trust deed that preserves only the estate the beneficiary would receive by survivorship does not incorporate separate properties.
material_facts: The disputed buildings had been acquired by earlier holders outside the geographical limits of the estate.
The buildings were used as residences, but the evidence did not show that estate business was conducted there or otherwise establish a clear intention to incorporate them.
The lower appellate court found the evidence of conduct ambiguous and the trial court’s contrary finding dependent on presumptions.
The trust deed settled the properties for the eldest son as he would receive them by inheritance or survivorship, and did not give him a greater estate than that mode of devolution would provide.
issues.conclusion: The buildings were not proved to have been incorporated into the impartible estate and remained partible.
issues.legal_principle: Under Shiba Prasad Singh v. Rani Prayag Kumari Debi, incorporation of immovable property requires proof of the holder’s intention, which may be inferred from conduct but cannot rest on presumption alone. The party asserting incorporation bears the burden of establishing it. The trust deed’s provision that the beneficiary receive the same estate as he would have obtained by survivorship did not enlarge the impartible estate or incorporate otherwise partible properties.

rule.if: partition_proceeding and acquired_immovable_buildings and incorporation_intention_not_proved and evidence_of_use_is_ambiguous and trust_deed_preserves_only_inherited_or_survivorship_interest

predicates.partition_proceeding: The dispute is being determined in a proceeding seeking partition of family property.
predicates.acquired_immovable_buildings: The disputed buildings were acquired as immovable property outside the original estate.
predicates.incorporation_intention_not_proved: The party claiming incorporation did not establish that the holder intended to make the buildings part of the impartible estate.
predicates.evidence_of_use_is_ambiguous: The buildings' use and the surrounding conduct do not clearly show that they were treated as part of the estate.
predicates.trust_deed_preserves_only_inherited_or_s: The trust deed gives the beneficiary no greater interest than the interest that would pass by inheritance or survivorship.

issues.definition: Buildings remain partible when their use does not clearly prove incorporation and the trust arrangement preserves only the interest that would otherwise pass by inheritance or survivorship.
